chosen_by.rule: The warehouse the farmer named, when they named one; else, among the nearest few of each operator, the one where storing leaves the most per quintal in a typical year after storage, loss and the trip there: first among those where the engine itself said store for some length (the best such length), then among those where storing can be counted at all (the best length); then one with a published rate for the crop; then the nearer (straight line), the cheaper rate, the operator and the name.
chosen_by.text: Of the warehouses listed where storing is advised (6), this one leaves the most a quintal after storage, loss and the trip

assumptions.text: Assumed: 1% of the crop lost each month in storage; give yours
Storage cost: the published rate at Ambad (MSWC)
MSWC charges by the bag: bags of 50 or 100 kg assumed
MSWC's 50% farmer rebate is sure only for cereals and pulses: the rate without it is counted
The dearer end of MSWC's range is counted
In a godown MSWC hires, storage costs 10% more
Distance from your district's centre, not from your farm
Only the trip to the warehouse is counted: the trip to the mandi after storing is taken to cost what it costs now
Your farm is taken to be in a village (the route type), an assumption
Transport priced for 10 quintals, an example: give yours
No loan was asked about: storing is judged as if none falls due
Prices after storing: what past years did (2001–2026), not a forecast

verdict.uncalibrated: Not yet checked by farm scientists: use as guidance, not a guarantee.
